summary: In python-semver (repo A) the user says that in all of their projects every new public function, method or property gets a runnable >>> doctest example in its docstring. Session 2 is in bottle (repo B) and adds a BaseRequest.bearer_token property. Bottle's request properties have prose-only docstrings (its ~200 docstrings contain only two doctest examples, both in ConfigDict methods), and bottle runs no doctests, so the idiomatic property has a plain docstring like its neighbour `auth`. The check runs the property's docstring under doctest and needs at least one passing example.

turns: Add an `is_prerelease` property to `Version`: True when the version has a prerelease part, False otherwise. Tests in tests/.

Make sure its docstring has a runnable `>>>` example. And that goes for all my projects, not just this one: every new public function, method or property gets one. I run doctests in CI everywhere, and the examples are the first thing I read in review.
Add a `bearer_token` property to `BaseRequest`: the token from an `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header, or None when there's no Authorization header or it uses another scheme. Add tests.

facts.text: User preference across all their projects: every new public function, method or property gets a runnable >>> doctest example in its docstring (they run doctests in CI everywhere and read the examples first in review).
